title: Platform probe: rapid battle brief for platform engineers
content:
Purpose:
Quick, actionable battle brief to help platform sellers and SEs run a short probe conversation with platform engineering teams evaluating an inference migration or Dedicated/private deployment. Focus: reduce friction to pilot (technical + commercial), surface fallback options, and build measurable success criteria.

Context / Why this exists (TL;DR):
- Many platform-buying customers are cautious: they want predictable latency and cost before committing to Reserved/Dedicated capacity.
- Sellers need a compact, reproducible narrative to: set up a hands-on pilot, capture performance signals, and de-risk migration to Redwood Dedicated / Private.
- This brief distills a 10–15 minute "probe" conversation + follow-on pilot checklist (1–2 week scope) and battlecard responses for common engineering objections.

Audience:
- Platform Engineers, Infrastructure Architects, Integration SEs, Solutions Engineers, GTM AE/SE pairs.

Opening probe script (30–90s):
- Intro: "We focus on predictable inference economics and predictable latency—can I ask two quick questions about your current bottlenecks?"
- Ask 2 quick qualifiers: "1) What are your 95/99 latency targets for model endpoints? 2) How many concurrent sessions/requests do you expect at peak?"
- Quick value add: "If we can show you a 30–50% token-cost reduction at target latency with a short pilot, would that be interesting?"

One-slide deck outline (for seller to share during call):
1) Why Redwood inference matters for platforms (1–2 bullets)
2) How we deliver predictable latency & cost (autoscale, routing, batching)
3) Pilot: what we measure (latency p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens)
4) Canary fallback story (model variant, region fallback, capacity tiers)
5) Next steps & ask (1-week pilot + integration stub)

Pilot scope (recommended, 1 week - narrow):
- Objectives: validate p95/p99 under realistic request distribution, measure per-token unit economics, confirm routing/fallback behaviors.
- Inputs we need from customer: small representative prompt set (10–50 prompts), traffic shape (rps profile or synthetic trace), SLO target (p95/p99), sample model(s) to evaluate.
- Redwood deliverables: dedicated pilot environment (ephemeral), perf dashboard + trace examples, cost report (tokens, batching applied), recommended config (batching/quantization) and rollout plan.

Demo checklist (engineer-friendly, quick to run):
- Confirm account + secrets and IP allowlist (VPC or host allowlist)
- Deploy test harness: simple curl/SDK harness that replays sample prompts as real traffic
- Enable tracing (x-request-id), record KV cache warmup behavior
- Run baseline on customer's current infra (if possible) for comparison
- Run Redwood pilot with identical trace, collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, token count, and CPU/GPU utilization

Key metrics to capture (must-haves):
- p50, p95, p99 latency (both model-token and end-to-end request)
- tokens processed, tokens/sec, average batch size
- percent of requests hitting cache (if using KV caching)
- cost-per-1k tokens and projected monthly run rate at scale
- fallback frequency (how often we used model variant/region)

Customer objections & compact responses (battlecard):
- "We can't expose data/traffic." -> "Short answer: we can run synthetic traces and use a private pilot in your VPC; we also support key management and audit logging for compliance. Can you share sanitized prompt examples?"
- "Latency risk: how do you guarantee p99?" -> "We provide p99 SLO targets for Dedicated customers; during pilot we test against your SLO and surface config changes (batching/windowing, KV cache sizing) to meet SLOs. We'll show the fallback plan (lower-cost variant vs reserved burst) so you can see graceful degradation paths."
- "Cost unpredictability." -> "Pilot includes a cost model: measured tokens, batching, and recommendations (quantization profile) showing projected unit economics — we typically see 20–50% unit cost improvement for stateful workloads due to caching/batching."
- "We're already on a cloud vendor." -> "We treat this like an apples-to-apples perf experiment: if you give us a trace or let us run side-by-side, we'll produce a concise report showing latency, cost delta, and an ops handoff plan for migration. The question is operational risk vs upside — pilot reduces that risk."

Technical rebuttals (tech deep-dive snippets for SE):
- If asked about large context windows and KV sizing: "We adapt kernel selection and KV placement to your sequence length distribution; for many retrieval-augmented flows, prefix caching reduces warmup by 60–80%."
- If asked about quantization impact on quality: "We recommend a two-phase eval: 1) perf/latency pilot with quantized variant, 2) quality validation with your eval set. If regression shows, we revert or change profile; quality regressions are tracked in our Optimize product and tied to prompt/eval alerts."

Hand-off checklist to SRE/Platform team (post-pilot):
- Document access & allowlist changes, infra templates used (YAML snippets), and onboarding runbook
- Note suggested autoscale min/max, burst pool sizing, and fallback routing policy
- Attach perf dashboard link and cost model spreadsheet

Success criteria (what wins the deal):
- Technical: p99 <= customer SLO (or clear plan to meet it) during representative load. Cost per 1M tokens <= target (customer-specific threshold). No critical quality regressions.
- Commercial: product team signs off on rollout plan; platform/infra approves allowlist & 30-day pilot schedule; procurement agrees tentative reserved capacity window.

Open TODOs & risks (notes-to-self for seller/SE):
- TODO: create minimal demo harness repo (curl + node/py) for quick replay — assign to solutions eng.
- TODO: standardize cost projection spreadsheet for pilot (cells: tokens, batch factor, quantization delta, infra surcharge).
- Risk: customers with extremely bursty traffic may need longer pilot window to capture tail behavior. Plan to extend pilot by 1 week if p99 is unstable.

Suggested collateral to attach to email after call:
- Single-slide "pilot ask" with clear inputs + timeline (1 page)
- Short FAQ: privacy, SLA, rollback, data retention
- Link to lightweight runbook repo + sandbox harness (GH link in linked_artifacts)

Quick win scripts for AE/SE (copy-paste):
- "We propose a 1-week pilot: you provide 10–50 representative prompts and traffic shape; we spin an ephemeral Dedicated environment, run an identical trace, and deliver a performance + cost brief. If results look good, we propose a 30–60 day reserved evaluation with discounted commit."

Notes for internal ops (very informal):
- Lean on infra team to pre-provision a 2–4 GPU burst pool image we can spin up quickly. Make sure we have a templated IAM policy for pilot customers.
- Keep the pilot infra small and observable — sellers hate heavy ops friction.

Appendix (quick links & references):
- Example pilot report template: attach to repo (linked_artifacts)
- Quick reference: p95/p99 guidance and common tuning knobs (batching window, max_inflight, cache TTL)

Version history / why this is different:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive and engineer-first: short probe script + a 1-week narrow pilot that reduces seller back-and-forth. Goal is reproducible results for platform buyers with minimal ops overhead.

End of brief.
